question.worked_solution:
Recall that by definition, $\text{nullity}(W)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(W)).$

To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(W))$, we reduce $W$ to row echelon form, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}W & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 12 & 4 & 9 \\ 5 & -20 & 10 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 10 & 18 \\ 5 & -20 & 10 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 10 & 18 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and  $1$
 non-pivot column (the $2$nd). 

Therefore,

$$
\text{nullity}(W)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(W))=1.
$$
